details:
Issues with "selfie expression" webcam hand tracking has been around for year now, I already described it here: https://feedback.vrchat.com/avatar-30/p/hands-freeze-in-weird-positions-if-using-sefie-expression-desktop-webcam-trackin

Sometimes it can be brief and last less than a second but shortly after the hand tries to return to some weird position again and overall these fits of tracking anomalies may last for hours, ultimately for a whole day. Whether it's moments when your avatar "waves" to someone you weren't trying to greet or cases when your arms twist and ruin a good picture in the last moment or when your arms block your entire vision mid-game and make you look as if you're having a stroke, these anomalies sometimes literally make you regret there's desktop tracking at all - and it's a feature that I was actually really excited about.

For cases when FBT VR tracking is acting up there is already a calibration feature with a famous T-pose and while webcam tracking obviously utilizies completely different kind of hardware I was wondering if it is possible to make some sort of calibration algorithm for webcam tracking as well. Maybe some sort of set of different hand positions to show into the camere as if to "tell" the system: that's how it looks when hands are down, that's my left hand, that's my right one, etc. Is it technically possible to make some sort of calibration task that would make camera look for some reference poses or other way to make it hallucinate less?

I believe I've heard in some recent dev video that there should be improvements to selfie expression coming so I'm hoping to see some in the future.
title: Webcam tracking calibration?
